title: The Elephant in the Room
summary: Lindy finds a very big elephant in her room, but nobody except her believes it is there. A story about friendship and believing in what you see.
pages:
One morning Lindy found an elephant in her room.
"Look!" she called. "There's an elephant in my room!"
"There's no elephant there," her mother called back. "Elephants don't live in houses. Everyone knows that."
The elephant yawned.

At breakfast Lindy's father asked her to pass the milk.
"I can't," said Lindy. "The elephant drank it all."
"There is no elephant," said her father. "Elephants don't live in the city. Everyone knows that."
The elephant burped.

At school the teacher grumbled, "What happened to this board? It's all crumpled!"
"That's not the board. That's my elephant!" said Lindy.
"There are no elephants at school," said the teacher. "Everyone knows that."
The elephant ate the teacher's sandwiches.

At recess the elephant followed Lindy to the playground.
It knocked over the swings by accident.
"Go away!" said Lindy. "You're not real and you shouldn't be here! Everyone knows that!"
The elephant hung its head. It walked away, wiping its eyes with its trunk.

After school Lindy couldn't see the elephant anywhere.
"Elephant!" she called. "Where are you?"

Lindy went home without it.
She felt lonely.
So she went outside, sat down on the steps and waited.
And waited.
And waited.

Then... she saw a trunk.
And tusks.
And ears.
The elephant was coming down the street!

She ran to it and hugged it.
"I'm sorry," she said. "I didn't mean it! I know you're real. You're my elephant."

The elephant lifted her up and set her on its back, and she rode it down the street.
She waved to her neighbors.
"Hello, Mr. Green! Hello, Mrs. Green!"
"Look at Lindy!" said Mr. Green. "How did she get up there? Maybe she grew!"
"Don't talk nonsense," said Mrs. Green. "Little girls don't grow that tall. Everyone knows that."

The elephant took Lindy to the lake, and she slid down its trunk like a slide.
"Wheee!" she squealed.
They played all afternoon, laughing and splashing and spraying water at each other.

At night the elephant tucked her into bed.
"Good night, Elephant," said Lindy. "Thank you for a wonderful day."
It patted her head, and curled up to sleep outside her window.
"Elephants are the best friends in the world," Lindy said to herself. "Nobody knows that, except me and my elephant."
